title.en: After the Key Went Down the Drain

dek.zh: 计划有一个谁都绕不过去的洞，天一亮，时间窗口就要关上：再等，可能永远没机会；现在动手，门却未必打得开。
dek.en: The plan had a hole no one could get around, and at daybreak the window would close. Wait, and the chance might never come again. Move now, and the gates might not open.

paras.zh: 正月十六日夜，北京。徐有贞家里聚着一伙密谋拥立太上皇复位的人，他们必须在天亮前决定动不动手。他们的计划有个洞：手里没有皇宫的钥匙，而夜里宫门不会开。可如果等到天亮，朝会上的一份奏折，可能让这个计划再也用不上。
paras.en: Beijing, the night of the sixteenth day of the first lunar month. A group of men sat in Xu Youzhen's house, plotting to put a retired emperor back on the throne, and they had to decide before dawn whether to move. Their plan had a flaw. They held no keys to the palace, and at night the palace gates did not open. Yet if they waited until morning, a memorial about to go before the court might leave their plan with nothing left to do.

paras.zh: 下面的故事依据当年明月《明朝那些事儿》的讲述。这本书写得像小说，不少人物心理和场面是作者的演绎，下文凡涉及心思和评价，都按书里的说法转述。
paras.en: The story that follows comes from Those Things of the Ming Dynasty (Mingchao naxie shir), a popular history by the writer known as Dangnian Mingyue. The book reads like a novel, and much of what its characters think and many of its scenes are the author's own dramatisation. Wherever this piece describes what someone was thinking, or how they should be judged, it is passing on what the book says.

paras.zh: 被关在南宫的是太上皇朱祁镇。关他的人是他的弟弟、在位皇帝朱祁钰，到这时已经关了七年。此时朱祁钰病得很重，又没有儿子，朝中多数大臣主张复立朱祁镇的儿子朱见深为继承人。
paras.en: The man held in the Southern Palace was the retired emperor, Zhu Qizhen. His jailer was his own younger brother, the reigning emperor Zhu Qiyu, who by now had kept him there for seven years. The reigning emperor was gravely ill and had no son. Most ministers at court wanted to reinstate the retired emperor's son, Zhu Jianshen, as heir.

paras.zh: 密谋的发起人是武将石亨。书里交代了他的动机：北京保卫战后，石亨受封侯爵，功劳最大的于谦只得了个虚名。石亨心里不安，便上书保举于谦的儿子于冕做官，没想到于谦对朱祁钰说：「石亨身为大将，却保举私人，应予惩戒」。书里说，石亨从此认定于谦不可能成为他的朋友；而于谦的靠山是朱祁钰，要对付于谦，就得先解决朱祁钰。后来病重的朱祁钰召石亨代为祭祀，石亨觉得机会来了。
paras.en: The plot began with a general, Shi Heng, and the book explains his motive. After the defence of Beijing, Shi Heng was made a marquis. Yu Qian, whose contribution had been the greatest, received only an empty honorific. Uneasy at the imbalance, Shi Heng sent up a memorial recommending Yu Qian's son, Yu Mian, for office. To his surprise, Yu Qian told the emperor Zhu Qiyu: "Shi Heng, a senior general, is recommending his private connections for office; he should be disciplined." From then on, the book says, Shi Heng was convinced that Yu Qian could never be his friend. Yu Qian's backer was Zhu Qiyu, so dealing with Yu Qian meant first dealing with the emperor. Later the ailing Zhu Qiyu summoned Shi Heng to perform the sacrificial rites in his place, and Shi Heng saw his opening.

paras.zh: 石亨管着京城防务和内城城门。他找来两个同谋：宦官曹吉祥，以及张辅的弟弟张軏。三个人凑到一起，眼看事情要泡汤，石亨便去请教老熟人、太常寺卿许彬。许彬说自己老了，干不了这种高风险的事，但可以推荐一个人，「只要这个人肯参加，大事必成」。他推荐的就是徐有贞。
paras.en: Shi Heng controlled the capital's defences and the gates of the inner city. He brought in two accomplices: Cao Jixiang, a eunuch, and Zhang Yue, a man of weighty family as the younger brother of Zhang Fu. Even with the three of them together, the scheme looked set to fall apart. So Shi Heng went for advice to Xu Bin, an old acquaintance who headed the Court of Imperial Sacrifices. Xu Bin said he was too old for such a dangerous line of work but could recommend someone: "As long as this man agrees to join, the great enterprise will succeed." The man he named was Xu Youzhen.

paras.zh: 在书里，徐有贞是个憋着一口气的人。当年明月写道，他眼光独到、很有才干，却因为说错一句话被众人唾弃；书中提到，九年前他夜观天象，准确预测了土木堡的失败，这次预测却给他带来侮辱和排挤。如今他虽已身居高位，当年的羞耻始终挂在心头，「他要讨回属于他的公道」。
paras.en: In the book, Xu Youzhen is a man nursing a grievance. Dangnian Mingyue writes that he had sharp judgement and real ability, yet everyone had reviled him for one wrong remark. Nine years earlier, the book recounts, he had read the night sky and correctly foretold the defeat at Tumu. That accurate prediction brought him humiliation and exclusion rather than credit. He now held high office, but the old shame never left him: "he meant to reclaim the justice that was his due."

paras.zh: 徐有贞一参加会议，就指出当务之急是和南宫里的朱祁镇取得联系。书里的解释很直白：你们就算除掉朱祁钰，也不可能自己做皇帝。没有朱祁镇点头，这件事就没有名分。三人这才派人去联络。那天是正月十三日，计划正式确定。
paras.en: The moment Xu Youzhen joined their meetings, he pointed out that the first priority was to reach Zhu Qizhen in the Southern Palace. The book gives the reasoning bluntly: even if they got rid of Zhu Qiyu, none of them could make himself emperor. Without the retired emperor's consent, the whole enterprise had no legitimacy. Only then did the three send someone to contact him. It was the thirteenth day of the first month, and the plan was formally settled.

paras.zh: 正月十四日早晨，朝会。病重的朱祁钰坚持到场，因为这次要议的是继承人。多数大臣主张复立朱见深；朱祁钰的亲信、大学士王文和陈循坚决反对，说宁可到外面找个藩王，也不要复立朱见深。双方吵成一团。朱祁钰只下了一道谕令：「我现在染病，十七日早朝复议。」又补了一句，书中引的原话是「所请不允」，意思是你们请求的事，不准。这句话驳回了复立朱见深，却没有定下继承人，事情被推到了三天以后。
paras.en: On the morning of the fourteenth, the court assembled. Ill as he was, Zhu Qiyu insisted on attending, because the question before it was the succession. Most ministers favoured reinstating Zhu Jianshen. The grand secretaries Wang Wen and Chen Xun, the emperor's confidants, flatly objected. Better, they said, to bring in some prince from an outlying fief than to restore Zhu Jianshen. The hall descended into argument. Zhu Qiyu issued a single decree: "I am now ill; this will be discussed again at the morning court on the seventeenth." Then he added a phrase that the book gives in its original form, suo qing bu yun: "what you request is not granted." With those words he turned down Zhu Jianshen's reinstatement without naming any heir, and pushed the whole matter back three days.

paras.zh: 当夜在石亨家，徐有贞先问朱祁镇知不知道，石亨说他已经同意了。徐有贞随即说出三步计划：第一步，借边关报警的消息，让都督张軏带一千军队进京；第二步，用石亨保管的钥匙打开内城城门，放这一千人进来作后备和警戒；第三步，去南宫接出朱祁镇，带他进大内宫城，趁朱祁钰病重宣布复位。问题在于，石亨只管内城城门，他们没有南宫和大内宫城的钥匙。书里说，这座宫城就是清代所称的紫禁城，「没有皇帝的命令，夜间宫城城门是绝不会开的」；真要硬攻，一闹出声响，侍卫和城防部队立刻就会赶到。
paras.en: That night, at Shi Heng's house, Xu Youzhen first asked whether Zhu Qizhen knew. He did, Shi Heng said, and he had agreed. Xu then laid out a plan in three steps. First, use a report of alarm on the frontier as cover for Zhang Yue, then a military commissioner, to lead a thousand troops into the capital. Second, open the inner-city gates with the keys Shi Heng kept and bring the thousand men inside as a reserve and a guard. Third, go to the Southern Palace, bring out Zhu Qizhen, escort him into the inner palace and, while Zhu Qiyu lay gravely ill, proclaim his restoration. The trouble was that Shi Heng controlled only the inner-city gates. They had no keys to the Southern Palace or to the inner palace. That palace, the book explains, is the one the Qing later called the Forbidden City, and "without the emperor's order, the palace gates would never open at night." If they tried to storm it, the noise would bring guards and garrison troops at once.

paras.zh: 当年明月相信，以徐有贞的聪明，应该看得出这个洞。他给的解释是：徐有贞不是嫌命长，而是觉得人生太短，短到不愿再忍耐、再等待，「是死是活，就赌这一把」。南宫那边，书里写朱祁镇也清楚风险很大，一旦出错，连囚徒都做不成，但他毫不犹豫地同意了，因为他别无选择。
paras.en: Dangnian Mingyue believes that a man as clever as Xu Youzhen must have seen the hole. In his explanation, Xu was not careless of his life. Rather, life seemed to him too short, so short that he would no longer endure or wait: "live or die, stake everything on this one throw." In the Southern Palace, the book says, Zhu Qizhen also knew how great the risk was. If it failed, he could not even go back to being a prisoner. He agreed anyway, without the slightest hesitation, because he had no other choice.

paras.zh: 正月十六日早晨，于谦、胡濙、王直商定，推举朱见深复立为太子，请商辂起草奏折，准备第二天朝会上提出。当年明月认为，朱祁钰无子又垂危，很可能会同意；到那时，朱祁镇就只能和自己的儿子抢皇位，阴谋再无用处。当夜，密谋者全部聚到徐有贞家，平日骄横的石亨等人慌了神，都看着徐有贞。书里写，徐有贞在屋里踱了一阵步，说：「我要去看一下天象。」他登上房顶，心里清楚天象不过是糊弄人的东西，最后作出决定：「成大事就在今晚，机不可失，动手！」出门时，他对送行的家人留下一句：「若回来，就做人，不能回来，便是鬼」。
paras.en: On the morning of the sixteenth, Yu Qian, Hu Ying and Wang Zhi agreed to propose that Zhu Jianshen be reinstated as crown prince. They asked Shang Lu to draft a memorial for the next day's court. Dangnian Mingyue reckons that Zhu Qiyu, sonless and dying, would very likely have accepted it. Zhu Qizhen would then have had to fight his own son for the throne, and the plot would have lost its purpose. That night every conspirator gathered at Xu Youzhen's house. Shi Heng and the others, usually so overbearing, lost their nerve and looked to Xu. In the book's telling, Xu paced the room for a while and then said: "I am going to look at the heavens." He climbed onto his roof, knowing full well that reading the stars was nothing but a way of fooling people, and there he made his decision: "The great deed is tonight. The moment must not be lost. We move!" As he left, he gave the family who had gathered to see him off one sentence: "If I come back, I'll be a man; if I don't, I'll be a ghost."

paras.zh: 长安门的钥匙由石亨掌管。他放张軏的一千军队进了内城，关上城门，然后慌了。书里说出了他慌的理由：这一千人并不知道自己是来造反的，随时可能哗变；只要被人发现，哪怕还没动手，他也逃不脱谋反的罪名。徐有贞对他说：「门锁好了吗，把钥匙给我吧。」石亨满腹狐疑，还是交了钥匙。徐有贞接过来，扔进了阴沟。石亨冲上去揪住他的衣服，问他是不是疯了。徐有贞答：「有进无退，有生无死」。
paras.en: The key to the Chang'an Gate was in Shi Heng's charge. He let Zhang Yue's thousand men into the inner city, shut the gate behind them, and then panicked. The book spells out why. The soldiers had no idea they had been brought in to stage a rebellion, and they might mutiny at any moment. If they were discovered, Shi Heng would be guilty of treason before anything had even happened. Xu Youzhen said to him: "Is the gate locked? Give me the key." Puzzled and suspicious, Shi Heng handed it over. Xu took the key and threw it into the drain. Shi Heng lunged at him, grabbed his robe and demanded to know whether he had gone mad. Xu answered: "Only forward, no retreat; only life, no death."

paras.zh: 据书中描写，就在这时，原本星月明亮的夜空突然暗了下来。石亨和张軏担心这是上天不让他们动手，站住了脚。徐有贞逼问为什么还不走，张軏小声问「事济否」，意思是事情能成吗。徐有贞走到他面前低吼「必济」：一定能成。张軏问的是胜算，徐有贞回的是一个不容商量的结论，没有给出新的理由。
paras.en: As the book describes it, at that very moment the starry, moonlit sky suddenly went dark. Shi Heng and Zhang Yue feared it was a sign that Heaven did not want them to act, and they stopped where they stood. Xu Youzhen demanded to know why they were not moving. Zhang Yue asked in a small voice, shi ji fou: "Will it succeed?" Xu walked up to him and growled, low, bi ji: "It will." Zhang Yue was asking about the odds. Xu answered with a verdict that was not open to discussion, and he offered no new reason.

paras.zh: 到了南宫，宫门紧闭，叫门也没人应答。徐有贞说：「不用叫门，把墙撞开就是了」。军士用木桩撞开宫墙，书中引的原话是「毁墙入」，朱祁镇被接了出来。到了东华门，守卫不开门，他们也没有钥匙。书里解释，南宫偏僻，拆了也没人追究；东华门是大内重地，有专人看守，一有动静就会引来侍卫。石亨看着徐有贞，徐有贞这次也沉默了。好话说尽，守门人不理，天眼看就要亮了。这时朱祁镇大喊一声，书中引的原话是「我太上皇也」：我是太上皇，开门！东华门开了。
paras.en: At the Southern Palace the gates were shut tight, and no one answered their calls. Xu said: "No need to call at the gate; just knock the wall down." The soldiers rammed the palace wall with timbers until it gave way. The book records this in the original words hui qiang ru, "broke the wall and went in", and Zhu Qizhen was brought out. At the Donghua Gate, however, the guards would not open, and the conspirators had no key. The book explains why the two gates were different. The Southern Palace was out of the way, and no one would come after them for a broken wall there. The Donghua Gate guarded the heart of the inner palace and had its own dedicated watch, and the slightest disturbance would bring the guards. Shi Heng turned to Xu Youzhen, and this time Xu, too, had nothing to say. They pleaded through the gate, the gatekeepers ignored them, and dawn was almost upon them. Then Zhu Qizhen let out a great shout, recorded in the book as wo taishanghuang ye: "I am the retired emperor. Open the gate!" The Donghua Gate opened.

paras.zh: 朱祁镇走向奉天殿，敲响上朝的钟鼓，宫城各门闻声开启。徐有贞独自挡在殿前，对闻讯赶来的内阁重臣说：「太上皇已经复位了，诸位还是快去祝贺吧」。书里还写，寝宫中的朱祁钰听到钟鼓，问左右是谁在敲，得知是哥哥在召集群臣，沉默片刻，笑着说了三个字：「好，好，好」。朱祁镇重新坐上了皇位。登基第二天，徐有贞入阁任兵部尚书，石亨封忠国公，张軏封太平侯，曹吉祥任司礼太监；书里说，就在同一天，徐有贞下令逮捕了于谦和王文等人。
paras.en: Zhu Qizhen walked to the Fengtian Hall and struck the bells and drums that summoned the court to audience. At the sound, the palace gates opened one after another. Xu Youzhen stood alone before the hall and told the senior grand secretaries who came hurrying at the news: "The retired emperor has already been restored. Gentlemen, you had better go and offer your congratulations." The book also describes Zhu Qiyu in his bedchamber, hearing the bells and drums and asking his attendants who was sounding them. Told that it was his elder brother summoning the ministers, he fell silent for a moment, then smiled and said only: "Good, good, good." Zhu Qizhen sat on the throne once more. On the second day after his restoration, Xu Youzhen entered the Grand Secretariat as minister of war, and Shi Heng was made Duke Zhongguo. Zhang Yue became Marquis of Taiping, and Cao Jixiang was made director of ceremonial eunuchs. On that same day, the book says, Xu Youzhen ordered the arrest of Yu Qian, Wang Wen and others.

heading.en: The Hole, the Window and the Shout

paras.zh: 徐有贞面对的，不只是“计划好不好”，还有“再等下去，还有没有计划可执行”。按书里的讲述，推他动手的力量有两股：一股是外部的，次日朝会一递上复立朱见深的奏折，密谋就失去意义；另一股是当年明月对他性格的推断，他不愿再等。前者是可以核对的时间压力，后者是作者的解释。不过，窗口紧迫只说明等待代价高，并不能证明计划行得通，东华门那个洞并没有因为时间紧而消失。
paras.en: Xu Youzhen faced more than the question of whether the plan was sound. He also had to ask whether, if he waited any longer, there would be any plan left to carry out. In the book's account, two forces pushed him to act. One came from outside: once the memorial to reinstate Zhu Jianshen reached the next morning's court, the plot would lose its point. The other is Dangnian Mingyue's reading of his character, which says he was no longer willing to wait. The first is a time pressure that can be checked against the sequence of events. The second is the author's interpretation. Still, a closing window shows only that waiting is costly. It does not prove the plan could work, and the hole at the Donghua Gate did not vanish because time was short.

paras.zh: 扔钥匙没有补上任何一个漏洞。它针对的是人：石亨怕的是还没动手就背上谋反罪名。城门此前已经关上，钥匙一没，城门就再打不开，这一千人也退不出去，收手这条路就断了，剩下的只有往前走。一种理解是，这一扔压住了同伴最危险的犹豫；但它也把一次可能的收手机会一并扔掉了。
paras.en: Throwing away the key filled none of the holes in the plan. It was aimed at people. Shi Heng's fear was being branded a traitor before anything had been done. The gate had already been shut behind the troops. With the key gone, the gate could not be reopened to send the men back out, so calling it off was no longer possible, and only the road forward remained. One reading is that the throw crushed the most dangerous hesitation among Xu's partners. But it also threw away a possible chance to pull back.

paras.zh: 最值得记住的，是两道门各自怎么开的。南宫靠撞墙，这是徐有贞临场补上的办法。东华门撞不得，他也无计可施，最后开门的是朱祁镇那一声“我是太上皇”。整件事里，朱祁镇的身份是唯一不需要钥匙的东西，而先和朱祁镇取得联系，恰恰是徐有贞一加入就坚持的第一步。所以，说他赢在计划周密并不准确，说他全凭运气也不全对：计划没能打开最后一道门，但他把一个能叫开门的人带到了门前。
paras.en: The detail most worth remembering is how each gate opened. The Southern Palace fell to a battered wall, an expedient Xu came up with on the spot. The Donghua Gate could not be battered, and Xu had no answer for it. What finally opened it was Zhu Qizhen's cry, "I am the retired emperor." In the whole affair, the retired emperor's standing was the one thing that needed no key. Reaching him was exactly the first step Xu had insisted on the moment he joined. So it is not quite right to say Xu won because his plan was meticulous, nor quite right to say he won on luck alone. His plan could not open the last gate, but he had brought to that gate the one man who could call it open.

paras.zh: 这场赌局也不宜当成励志故事来读。书里写，包括守门人在内的所有人都被朱祁镇这一声怒吼震住，东华门随之打开；而赌赢之后紧接着的，是封赏，以及对于谦的逮捕。
paras.en: Nor is this gamble best read as an inspirational tale. In the book, Zhu Qizhen's shout stunned everyone, the gatekeepers included, and the Donghua Gate swung open. What came straight after the winning throw was rewards, and the arrest of Yu Qian.

paras.zh: 全文只依据《明朝那些事儿》一本通俗历史读物。屋顶上的心思、天色突暗时众人的感受、朱祁钰听到钟鼓后的神情，都是书中的小说化写法；「所请不允」「事济否」「必济」「毁墙入」「我太上皇也」等短句，是书中引用的原话。
paras.en: This piece rests entirely on a single work of popular history, Those Things of the Ming Dynasty. Xu's thoughts on the rooftop, the conspirators' feelings when the sky went dark and Zhu Qiyu's expression when he heard the bells all belong to the book's novelistic writing. The short phrases suo qing bu yun, shi ji fou, bi ji, hui qiang ru and wo taishanghuang ye are what the book presents as original quoted wording.

paras.zh: 一次成功不能证明这种赌法对。这个故事能说明的，只是在窗口真的会关闭时，等待也有代价；以及成败可能落在计划之外的人身上。它说明不了断后路一定能换来胜利。
paras.en: One success does not prove that this kind of gamble is right. The story can show only two things: when a window really is closing, waiting has a cost too, and success or failure may rest on someone outside the plan. It cannot show that cutting off your own retreat will bring victory.

scenario.zh: 周四晚上，产品负责人小周得到消息：明早的评审会大概率会拍板竞争团队的方案。小周团队的方案还有一环没打通，与支付系统的对接要靠另一个部门配合，而对方负责人今晚联系不上。有同事提议连夜上线演示版，并把旧版回退分支删掉，“省得大家再摇摆”。
scenario.en: On Thursday evening, Zhou, a product lead, hears that tomorrow morning's review meeting will very probably sign off on a rival team's proposal. One link in Zhou's own team's proposal still isn't working. The integration with the payment system needs help from another department, and that department's lead can't be reached tonight. A colleague suggests pushing a demo version live overnight and deleting the old rollback branch, so that nobody wavers any more.

question.zh: 你会今晚强行推进吗？如果推进，要不要删掉回退分支？
question.en: Would you force it through tonight? And if you did, would you delete the rollback branch?

assumptions.zh: 明早拍板的消息基本可靠；支付对接今晚可能找到其他人临时处理，也可能找不到；演示失败只会丢掉这次机会，不会伤及现有业务。
assumptions.en: The news about tomorrow's decision is basically reliable. Someone else may or may not be found tonight to handle the payment integration temporarily. A failed demo would cost only this one opportunity and would not harm the existing business.

steps.zh: 先分清窗口是否真的会关：明早如果只是讨论，就不必赌。再找一找自己的“东华门”和“朱祁镇”：哪一环光靠计划打不开，有没有一个人或一项资源能在关键时刻打开它，今晚能不能先联系上。最后再定回退分支：如果团队的问题是犹豫，可以用明确分工和截止时间代替删分支；只有回退本身会拖垮执行时，才考虑切断。
steps.en: First, work out whether the window really will close. If tomorrow is only a discussion, there is no need to gamble. Next, look for your own Donghua Gate and your own Zhu Qizhen. Which link can planning alone not open? Is there a person or a resource who could open it at the critical moment, and can you reach them tonight? Only then decide about the rollback branch. If the team's problem is hesitation, a clear division of labour and a firm deadline can do that job instead of deleting the branch. Consider cutting it off only if the fallback itself would drag down execution.

alternative.zh: 不强推。明早在会上如实说明哪一环未通、需要几天，争取复议时间。朱祁钰把继承人一事推到三天后，也说明拖延本身就是一种选项。
alternative.en: Don't force it. At tomorrow's meeting, say plainly which link isn't working yet and how many days it needs, and ask for time before the decision is final. Zhu Qiyu's move to push the succession back three days is a reminder that delay is itself an option.

uncertainty_note.zh: 全部内容来自当年明月《明朝那些事儿》，叙述高度小说化，人物心理、部分对白和场面属作者演绎；作者对徐有贞冒险动机的解释是推断。文中只用书中的“正月某日”，未换算年份；此后各人的结局未写。
uncertainty_note.en: Everything here comes from Dangnian Mingyue's Those Things of the Ming Dynasty, a heavily novelised narrative. Characters' thoughts, some of the dialogue and some scenes are the author's dramatisation, and his explanation of why Xu Youzhen took the risk is an inference. Dates follow the book's days of the first lunar month and are not converted to a year. What later became of each person is not covered.

preheader.zh: 计划有个打不开的门，明早机会就没了——那一夜，他把唯一的钥匙扔进了阴沟。
preheader.en: The plan had a gate no one could open, and by morning the chance would be gone. That night, he threw the only key into the gutter.
